subject: environmental
audience: FE Environmental candidates and environmental engineering students
title: The Treatment Plant That Removed 4,379 lb/day, Not 210
featured_title: THE TREATMENT PLANT THAT REMOVED 4379 LB PER DAY, NOT 210

presentation.challenge: The concentration drop was 210 mg/L, but that was not a mass removal rate. At 2.5 MGD, the plant removed about 4,379 lb/day of BOD.

practice.primary_question: How are concentration, flow rate, mass loading, and treatment removal efficiency related?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Subtracting influent and effluent concentrations and reporting the numerical concentration difference as a mass removal rate.

case_dna.target_misconception: A concentration decrease of 210 mg/L means the plant removes 210 lb/day.
case_dna.why_plausible: The concentration difference is numerically simple and can be mistaken for a loading rate if flow units are ignored.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: Using loading=Q(MGD)×C(mg/L)×8.34, influent loading is 5004 lb/day and effluent loading is 625.5 lb/day, so 4378.5 lb/day is removed.
case_dna.corrected_model: Mass loading depends on both concentration and volumetric flow. Removal efficiency is based on the ratio of removed concentration or load to the influent value when flow is unchanged.

problem_statement: A wastewater plant treats 2.5 MGD. Influent BOD is 240 mg/L and effluent BOD is 30 mg/L. Assume the same flow rate at the inlet and outlet and use 8.34 as the lb/day conversion factor for MGD·mg/L. A note reports 210 lb/day removed because 240-30=210. Determine the influent load, effluent load, mass removed per day, and percent removal.

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: The concentration difference was correct. The mass removal rate was not.
gates.prompt: What quantity must multiply concentration before reporting lb/day?

options.label: Use load=Q×C×8.34 and compare inlet and outlet loads
options.reason: Mass loading requires both volumetric flow and concentration.

options.label: Use 240-30=210 and report 210 lb/day
options.reason: The subtraction produces mg/L, not lb/day.

options.label: Divide concentration by flow to obtain loading
options.reason: For the stated units, loading scales with flow rather than inversely with it.

gates.label: Predict
gates.heading: Predict the mass removed
gates.prompt: Enter the BOD mass removed in lb/day.

gates.label: Experiment
gates.heading: Close the plant mass balance
gates.result: The plant removes about 4,379 lb/day of BOD.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove the loading difference
gates.hint: The concentration difference must be multiplied by flow and the 8.34 conversion factor.

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the treatment-performance note
report: C3. Therefore BOD removal is 210 lb/day.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: It assigns mass-per-time units to a concentration difference and ignores flow.

evidence_choices.label: 2.5×210×8.34=4378.5 lb/day
evidence_choices.reason: This converts the concentration reduction at the stated flow into a mass removal rate.

correction.template: The plant removes about {removed_load} lb/day of BOD at {removal_efficiency}% efficiency.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Reach 90% BOD removal at the same influent concentration
gates.constraint: Keep influent BOD at 240 mg/L and assume the same inlet/outlet flow.

options.label: Reduce effluent BOD to 24 mg/L
options.reason: At 90% removal, 10% of 240 mg/L remains: 24 mg/L.

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply the same loading method
gates.prompt: A 1.2 MGD plant reduces a contaminant from 180 to 45 mg/L. What mass is removed per day?

options.label: 135 lb/day
options.reason: This is only the concentration difference expressed with the wrong units.

options.label: About 1,801 lb/day
options.reason: That does not match the stated flow-concentration conversion.

gates.explanation: For unchanged flow, removed loading is Q(Cin-Cout)×8.34.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the wastewater loading calculation
gates.confirmation: I confirm that mass loading requires both concentration and flow, and that removal efficiency is distinct from mass removed per day.

items.label: What failed
items.value: A concentration difference was labeled as a mass removal rate.

items.label: Corrected model
items.value: Use Q×C×8.34 for lb/day loading when Q is in MGD and C is in mg/L.

seo.seo_title: Wastewater BOD Loading and Removal Efficiency | FE Environmental E-071
seo.meta_description: Solve FE Environmental Case E-071: a 2.5 MGD plant reducing BOD from 240 to 30 mg/L removes about 4,379 lb/day at 87.5% efficiency.
seo.focus_keyphrase: FE Environmental BOD loading removal efficiency
seo.excerpt: A concentration reduction is not yet a mass removal rate. Flow converts mg/L into a daily contaminant load.
seo.direct_answer: Using load=Q(MGD)×C(mg/L)×8.34, the influent BOD load is 5004 lb/day and the effluent load is 625.5 lb/day. The plant removes 4378.5 lb/day, and the removal efficiency is 87.5%.

faqs.q: How do you calculate wastewater contaminant loading in lb/day?
faqs.a: For Q in MGD and C in mg/L, use load=Q×C×8.34.

faqs.q: What is the BOD removal efficiency from 240 to 30 mg/L?
faqs.a: 87.5% when inlet and outlet flow are the same.
